Surah 107: Al-Ma'un (The Small Kindnesses)

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah, the Exalted, says, censuring those who neglect His rights and the rights of His servants: {Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?} That is, denies the Resurrection and the Reckoning, and therefore does not believe in what the Messengers brought.

{2} {That is the one who repulses the orphan}, that is, pushes him away with harshness and severity, and shows him no mercy, because of the hardness of his heart and because he neither hopes for reward nor fears punishment.

{3} {And does not urge the feeding of the needy}: that is, he does not urge others {to feed the poor}. It follows all the more that he himself does not feed the poor.

{4-5} {So woe to those who pray}, that is, those who are committed to establishing the prayer, {but who are heedless of their prayer}: that is, they neglect it, delay it beyond its time, and fail to observe its pillars. This is due to their lack of concern for God's command, since they have wasted the prayer, which is the most important of the acts of worship. Heedlessness regarding the prayer is what deserves blame and reproach for its owner. As for forgetfulness within the prayer, it occurs to everyone, even to the Prophet (ﷺ).

{6-7} For this reason, Allah described these people with ostentation, hardness, and lack of mercy, saying: {Those who make show} (yurā'ūn), that is, they perform deeds for the sake of being seen by people, {and withhold small kindnesses} (al-ma'un), that is, they refuse to give out things whose lending or gifting causes no harm, such as a vessel, a bucket, an axe, and the like, which custom has made common to share and lend. These people, because of their extreme greed, withhold such small kindnesses; so how much more would they withhold what is greater than these?

In this surah there is an exhortation to feed orphans and the needy, and an urging to do so; to observe the prayer, guard it, and be sincere in it and in all other deeds; and to encourage doing good and giving away light things, such as lending a vessel, a bucket, a book, and the like, because Allah censured those who do not do so. And Allah, glorified is He, knows best.
